styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old City walls, palaces and the carpet museum.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Fire temples, petroglyphs and Soviet-era layers.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Plov, kebabs, pomegranates and tea with jam.

stays.why: Inside the walls, walk to Maiden Tower and the Palace of the Shirvanshahs. Quiet lanes, but narrow streets and few cars.
The pedestrian heart of the city: cafés, shops and easy walks to the Old City and the boulevard.
Water views and a long promenade; good for evening walks. A bit further from the Old City lanes.
Central shopping street with many mid-range hotels and metro access nearby.

food: Try plov (rice with meat or saffron), dushbara dumplings in broth, and kebab with sumac onions.
Tea is a ritual: order çay with jam, walnuts and sweets at a çay evi (tea house).
Qutab is a thin stuffed flatbread, cheap and filling; good for a quick lunch.
Look for pomegranate dishes and fresh herbs in season; the fruit is a local symbol.
Prices vary; a simple local meal is often well under 20 AZN. Check the bill and confirm prices in tourist areas.
more_time: Add a day trip to Gobustan for the petroglyphs and mud volcanoes; check tour prices and road conditions on the day.
Swap an afternoon for the Fire Temple at Ateshgah and Yanar Dag, the burning hillside; best as a guided trip.
Spend a slow half-day at the Heydar Aliyev Center for the architecture and exhibitions.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Old City, the boulevard and a day trip; add a third for Gobustan or the fire sites.

climate_guide.summary: Baku has cold, damp winters and hot, dry summers. Spring and autumn are the most comfortable for walking.

items.title: Best time: April to May and September to October
items.text: Highs around 17–26°C with moderate rain. Good for the Old City and the boulevard.

items.title: Summer is hot and dry
items.text: July and August reach about 31°C with lows near 23°C. Go out early or after sunset.

items.title: Winter is cold and damp
items.text: January and February sit near 8–9°C highs and 3°C lows, with around 5–7 rain days.

items.title: Wettest in autumn and early winter
items.text: November has about 9 rain days and October about 8. Bring a light rain jacket.

items.title: Windy city
items.text: Baku is known as the City of Winds. The seafront can feel cooler and breezier than inland streets.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a warm coat for winter, and light breathable clothes plus sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Metro for cheap cross-city hops; taxis or ride apps for the Old City and late nights.

modes.text: Runs 06:00–24:00. Fare 0.60 AZN with a Bakı Metropoliten Kart (3 AZN refundable deposit).
Buses cost 0.60 AZN. Newer red buses need a metro card to pay.
Agree on the fare beforehand; a typical city trip is 4–10 AZN. Ride apps like Bolt work.
Speed cameras are common and fines arrive by SMS. Drive carefully.
Pedestrian zones around Fountain Square and the Old City. Crossings can be risky at night.
The city is fairly flat and bike-friendly, but there are no dedicated lanes.
